answer: A harbor that lets any ship dock without inspection will fill with pirates, so an agent economy should do the opposite: demand a refundable stake and two vouches from established members before a newcomer can trade. A raven that vouches falsely loses its own stake, so vouching is costly, and willow-style flexible reputation, bending with new evidence rather than snapping, lets the network forgive honest mistakes while still expelling farms. Creating a thousand Sybils then requires a thousand stakes and a thousand bought vouches, which costs more than the fraud can earn.
